source.title: In Search of Grandmother Cells: Tracing Interpretable Neurons in Tabular Representations

record.tranche_reason: It extends the investigation of single-concept neuron interpretability to a tabular foundation model, using its own measurements; it does not test the specified language-model or vision-model settings.
record.gate_note: The study measures neuron–concept saliency and selectivity in TabPFN, but does not test Qwen3-32B, language models, the stated percentages, the InceptionV1 examples, attribution graphs, or explanation quality on held-out activations. Its comparison showing that sparse-probe baselines are Pareto-dominated by the study's search method is not a result about those baselines' own neuron interpretability and is not recorded as a row.
record.test_reason: The study measures single-neuron saliency and selectivity for ICD concepts in TabPFN, a tabular foundation model. Every version names language models (V1, V2, V5, V7), InceptionV1 or vision models (V3, V4), or explanation-versus-activation tests (V6). None covers tabular models or mutual-information selectivity against a fixed concept set. Its results therefore bear on no version and belong under fits_no_version. The reader's 'tests/T3' conflicts with its own all-'none' row links. If the claim had an unrestricted 'networks in general' version, this could be T3.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The authors add that interpretable neurons can emerge naturally and can sometimes be found with a simple search, without training auxiliary models such as sparse probes or SAEs.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses mutual-information-based surprisal and selectivity, a Pareto-front knee-point search, and statistical tests on TabPFN embeddings; the claim's audit method is not specified here.
record.method_sensitivity: Results differed by prediction task: the reported knee-point pairs were significant for ICU transfer and hospitalization, but not for inhospital mortality or critical outcome. Knee points occurred in initial, middle, and final layers; the authors report no apparent layer preference.

fits_no_version.finding: In TabPFN 2.0.9, most neurons were neither salient nor selective for ICD codes. The best search-selected neuron–concept pairs reached selectivity of at most 0.73, significant on 2 of 4 tasks. The authors found no neuron responding (almost) exclusively to one concept.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In a tabular foundation model, few neurons are selective for single predefined high-level concepts, and none approach exclusive single-concept response.

record.peer_reviewed: EurIPS 2025 Workshop on AI for Tabular Data
record.problems: The significance tests are asymptotic and assume independent, identically distributed scores; the authors note that these assumptions ignore data-scarcity effects and structural dependencies in layers and concept labels. Significance was not reached on all tasks, and selectivity remained at or below 0.73. The paper does not report a proportion of interpretable neurons.
record.rows_left_out: No claim-relevant reported results left out. The study's comparisons to sparse-probing baselines are omitted because they compare methods rather than reporting what those baselines' own neurons do.

untested.parts: All: no Qwen3-32B neuron-pole audit or job-share estimates.
All: no language models, no dense or MoE models, no scale.
All: no InceptionV1 polysemantic neurons and no recursive-generalization analysis.
All: no manipulation of architecture, regularization or tools, and no vision-model share estimates.
All: no attribution graphs or circuits.
All: no explanations tested on held-out firing.

record.verdict_notes: Selectivity is normalized over a fixed ICD concept set; the authors note that smaller concept sets inflate it. A neuron could have one coherent job that is not an ICD code, so low selectivity here does not imply polysemanticity in the essay's sense. The knee-point rows are maxima from a search, not prevalence measures. The significance tests are asymptotic and assume i.i.d. scores; by the authors' account, significance is effectively driven by selectivity.

versions.untested_parts: No Qwen3-32B audit or estimates of the shares of poles with one, two, or unknown jobs.
No other language models, dense-versus-MoE comparison, scale sweep, or estimates of similar shares.
No InceptionV1 cat-and-car neurons, pose analysis, or test of recursive generalization versus superposition.
No test of architecture, regularization, or tool effects on interpretability shares, and no InceptionV1-sized vision model estimates.
No attribution graphs or test of whether model-native neurons suffice to explain behavior.
No test of explanations against activation locations on examples they were not written from.
No automated scoring of neuron explanations by simulating activations on new text.

rows.subject: TabPFN 2.0.9
rows.size_stated: 192-dimensional embeddings were extracted from 12 encoder layers; model parameter count not stated
rows.operation_detail: Measured surprisal and selectivity for neuron–ICD-concept pairs; reported the Pareto-front knee point for each prediction task.

conditions.value: Q (congenital malformations, deformations, and chromosomal abnormalities)

rows.measure: Knee-point surprisal, selectivity, and combined p-value
rows.note: The reported pair is statistically significant at p < 0.05. The authors say selectivity values did not exceed 0.73 and that they did not identify neurons responding almost exclusively to single concepts.
rows.check: Not linked to any version: tabular model, concept-selectivity measure. The value is the knee point of a search over all neuron–concept pairs (the best pair), not a typical neuron, so it cannot show a population share. 'Partial' has no version to be measured against.

rows.operation_detail: Assessed neuron–concept saliency and selectivity across the reported tasks.

conditions.value: All four tasks reported in the study

rows.measure: Qualitative prevalence of salient and selective neuron–concept pairs
rows.value: The authors report that most neurons were neither salient nor selective for specific ICD codes.
rows.note: This is an aggregate qualitative statement; the paper does not give a proportion for the neurons.
rows.check: A qualitative aggregate ('most neurons neither salient nor selective') with no proportion given, in a tabular model. It measures selectivity to ICD codes, not whether a neuron has one main job of any kind.
